records.statement: Vinge's column “First Word” (Omni, January 1983) says that people will soon create intelligences greater than their own, and that human history will then reach a kind of singularity beyond which the world passes far beyond human understanding.
records.qualification: Earliest located within this increment's bounded search, which read Vinge (1983, 1993) and Ulam (1958), and the cross-family check's search (Good, Turing, Campbell, Descartes, Lucas, Dreyfus); not a claim that no earlier text exists. The column also considers a route through amplification of human intelligence by computers ('The singularity then becomes the result of a massive amplification of human intelligence'), which the criterion includes. Paraphrase only, as the dataset's source requires. The dataset already records this column on A1, A4 and B6 as context.

searchLog.searched: Vinge 1983 (Omni scan, page image); Vinge 1993 (NTRS text layer, pp. 11–22); Ulam 1958 (not reachable here; the cross-family check's reading used). Good 1965 was not reread against U03. The cross-family check (2026-11-04, A1.1, A1.2) also read Good (pp. 31–33), Ulam p. 5, Turing c. 1951, Campbell, The Last Evolution (a 2008 transcription of a later reprint), Descartes 1637 pp. 56–57, Lucas 1961 p. 112 and Dreyfus 1965 p. 6.
searchLog.earliestNote: Vinge (1983-01) is the earliest located articulation in these bounded searches; the checker agrees. Ulam (1958) is earlier but names no machines and is context. Good (dated 1965 in the dataset; the publisher's metadata says 1966) is a near match read by the checker as bearing on U03: it states an 'intelligence explosion' and a last invention, not a point beyond which human affairs could not continue or be foreseen. Contest: no text that disputes the singular transition itself was located. The checker reads Descartes (1637) as a qualified contest of a premise (that a constructed machine could reach general, human-like reason), which bears on the machine route only, not on amplified human intelligence; it is noted here and not recorded on U03. Earliest located means earliest found, not first; a negative search does not establish absence.
